topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and sets out the learning objectives regarding cancer therapy modalities.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy along with general mechanisms of drug toxicity and efflux-mediated resistance.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies that exploit cancer-specific vulnerabilities, such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failures, and synthetic lethality in defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on small-molecule inhibitors targeting oncogenic driver kinases and the molecular mechanisms underlying acquired drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address targeted antibody therapies that recognize cancer cell-surface antigens to inhibit oncogenic signaling, trigger cytotoxicity, or deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and cellular immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore tumor immune surveillance and advanced immunotherapeutic strategies that reactivate or engineer T cells to target cancer cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical perspectives, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate broader clinical challenges, historical mortality trends, and future paradigms in managing cancer and evaluating new therapeutics.
